extracted.intended_audience: publishers, newsroom editors, and content teams using Apple News / Apple News Publisher
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and signals Apple News uses to select and surface stories across Top Stories (human-curated), Trending (algorithmic), and For You (personalized) sections; intended to guide publishers on what is valued and what disqualifies content. Covers editorial standards, disqualifiers, algorithmic engagement signals, and implicit newsworthiness preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top Stories curated by human editors favor original reporting over aggregated copy; publishers should provide original journalism rather than simply compiling others' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factuality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories considered for Top Stories must be factually accurate; avoid publishing or syndicating content that spreads false or unverified claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free of bias / sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial curation disfavors biased or sensationalist presentation. Headlines and framing should not be one-sided or designed primarily to provoke an emotional reaction (avoid sensationalism/clickbait).

rubrics_metrics.name: Established publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple News editors prefer recognized publications with a track record of reliable journalism; new or unknown outlets may be less likely to be selected for Top Stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of reporting, writing, sourcing, and overall editorial standards are considered; strong journalistic craft increases chances of being chosen for Top Stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible publishers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only publishers that meet Apple’s eligibility/recognition standards are likely candidates for human-curated placement; being a recognized brand helps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hate speech (disqualifier)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content containing hate speech is a disqualifying factor for placement; such material will be excluded from featured sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination (disqualifier)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that discriminates against protected groups is disqualified from being featured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of Apple policies (disqualifier)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any content that breaches Apple News policies will be disqualified; publishers should ensure compliance with Apple’s rules and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensational or misleading headlines (disqualifier)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines that mislead or are deliberately sensational are disallowed for featured placement and may prevent stories from being selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click volume (Trending signal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithmic Trending section uses raw measures of user clicks (engagement volume) as a signal for which stories are trending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-through rates (Trending signal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How far users read into an article (read-through) is used as a signal for Trending — higher completion/engagement boosts algorithmic ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social engagement (Trending signal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social interactions (shares, likes, comments) contribute to algorithmic detection of trending stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency (Trending signal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness and how recent a story is are signals the Trending algorithm uses to surface current popular items.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-followed topics (For You signal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalized 'For You' recommendations factor in topics a user follows when surfacing stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-followed channels (For You signal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories from channels a user follows are more likely to appear in their For You feed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read history (For You signal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A user’s prior reading history influences personalization; the algorithm uses past behavior to infer interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic affinity (For You signal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broader measures of a user’s affinity for topics (beyond explicit follows) are used to recommend relevant stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand reputation as gatekeeper (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple’s brand and editorial role function as a gatekeeper; reputation can influence which sources and stories are prioritized across sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial preference for original reporting (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond explicit Top Stories criteria, editors implicitly favor original, reporting-driven work over aggregated content when making selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic preference for engagement (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm-driven areas (Trending, For You) favor engagement metrics (clicks, read-through, social signals) which can lead to different selections than human editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of sources (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity of sources (Apple editors known for source diversity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple News editors are known to prefer a diverse set of sources; editorial curation aims to represent multiple outlets rather than concentrating on a few.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of clickbait (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both editorial standards and disqualifying factors emphasize steering clear of clickbait-style content; truthful, contextual headlines are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic balance across sections (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors consider topical balance when curating sections—ensuring a mix of subject matter rather than overrepresenting a single topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-friendly format (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content optimized for mobile display (formatting, length, multimedia suitability) is implicitly favored for placement in Apple News.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual quality (implicit criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality visuals (images, video, layout) are part of the implicit criteria that improve a story’s suitability for featured placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection vs algorithmic selection (research note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human editors choose sources more evenly than algorithms; they prefer source diversity and contextual quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research indicates Apple News editors distribute selections across sources more evenly than algorithms, and place greater weight on contextual quality and source diversity versus raw engagement metrics.
